title: TOCIACS : Efficacy and safety of Tocilizumab for acute chest syndrome treatment in paediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease
official: TOCIACS : Efficacy and safety of Tocilizumab for acute chest syndrome treatment in paediatric and adult patients with sickle cell disease
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy over placebo of tocilizumab (single intravenous infusion at 8 mg/kg for patients ≥ 30 kg (up to a maximum of 800 mg) and 12 mg/kg for patients < 30 kg) on time to successful weaning from both supplemental oxygen and any respiratory support (non-invasive or invasive), in paediatric and adult Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) patients with Acute Chest Syndrome (ACS).

interventions.name: CHLORURE DE SODIUM 0,9 % B. BRAUN, solution injectable en ampoule

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. SCD patient of all genotypes (SS, SC, S/β0 and S/β+) or other major SCD syndrome
2. Age ≥ 2 years old
3. Hospitalised for ACS, defined by the WHO as the association of fever and/or acute respiratory symptoms with a new pulmonary infiltrate on chest imaging, (X-ray, lung ultrasound, or CT scan)
4. Requiring supplemental oxygen ≥ 2 L/min for SpO2 ≥ 95% or non-invasive respiratory support (high flow nasal oxygen or continuous positive airway pressure or bilevel non-invasive ventilation) or invasive mechanical ventilation or ECMO, for less than 48 hours
5. Negative pregnancy test for girls or women of childbearing age (15-50 years old)
6. Freely given, informed and written consent of patient or legal representatives
7. Affiliation to the social security (or health insurance)
8. Effective contraception up to 6 months after treatment administration
Exclusion criteria:
1. Impossibility to perform tocilizumab/placebo injection within the first 48 hours of supplemental oxygen ≥2L/min or for SpO2≥95% and/or respiratory support (as defined in inclusion criteria n°4). If exchange transfusion is indicated at inclusion, it has to be performed before the injection of tocilizumab/placebo.
2. Imminent and inevitable progression towards death in the opinion of the investigator
3. Absolute neutrophil count < 1.0 G/L or platelets < 50 G/L
4. ALT or AST > 5   fold the upper limit of normal
5. Glomerular Filtration rate (GFR) < 60 mL/min/1,73 m²)
6. History of bowel diverticulitis or gastrointestinal perforation
7. Immunomodulatory or anti-rejection therapy within the last 3 months
8. Current enrolment in another interventional research concerning a medicinal product for human use
9. Known hypersensitivity to tocilizumab or its excipients
10. Known active current severe bacterial, viral, fungal, mycobacterial, or other infections (including but not limited to tuberculosis and atypical mycobacterial disease, hepatitis B and C, and herpes zoster)
11. Immunization with a live/attenuated vaccine within the last 4 weeks
12. Immunomodulatory therapy, anti-rejection therapy, cell depleting therapies and investigational agents within the last 3 months
13. History of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to human, humanized, or murine monoclonal antibodies
14. History of diverticulitis, diverticulosis requiring antibiotic treatment, or chronic ulcerative lower gastrointestinal disease such as Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, or other symptomatic lower gastrointestinal conditions that might predispose a patient to perforations
15. Evidence of malignant disease or malignancies diagnosed within the last 3 years
16. Pregnancy or breastfeeding
